subject: social-studies
title: Foundations of High School United States History and Geography
essential_question: How do historians and geographers build defensible claims about the American past?
performance_task: Build a sourcing-and-corroboration casebook that tests one claim about American founding ideals against primary and secondary evidence.
anchor_sources: Declaration of Independence (National Archives)
Constitution of the United States and its amendments (National Archives)
Northwest Ordinance of 1787 (Avalon Project)

subject: social-studies
title: Industrial and Urban America, 1870-1900
essential_question: How did industrial growth reshape where and how Americans lived and worked?
topics: western settlement and federal Indian policy
performance_task: Produce a multi-source causal analysis of how industrial growth reshaped work, cities, and migration, using at least one data set and one firsthand account.
anchor_sources: United States Census reports, 1870-1900 (U.S. Census Bureau)
Dawes Act of 1887 (National Archives)
Detroit Publishing Company photograph collection (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Becoming a World Power and World War I
essential_question: Why and how did the United States become a world power, and what did that shift cost?
topics: growth of United States global power
causes of World War I and American entry
the domestic impact of World War I
the Fourteen Points and the peace settlement
performance_task: Write an evidence-based position paper on the League of Nations debate that names and fairly represents at least two period positions.
anchor_sources: Treaty of Versailles, 1919 (Avalon Project)
Congressional Record, League of Nations ratification debate, 1919-1920 (U.S. Government Publishing Office, govinfo.gov, and HathiTrust)
Espionage Act of 1917 and Sedition Act of 1918 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: The Progressive Era
essential_question: Whose problems did Progressive reform solve, and whose did it leave unsolved?
topics: regulation and the role of government
exclusions and limits of Progressive reform
performance_task: Evaluate the Progressive Era with a claim, a named counterclaim, and an evidence set that addresses both achievements and exclusions.
anchor_sources: Sixteenth, Seventeenth, Eighteenth, and Nineteenth Amendments (National Archives)
Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906 (National Archives)
National American Woman Suffrage Association records (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Boom, Depression, and the New Deal
essential_question: What caused the Great Depression, and how far did the New Deal change the role of government?
topics: social and cultural change in the 1920s
the changing role of the federal government
performance_task: Build a data-and-testimony exhibit explaining Depression causes and evaluating New Deal responses with cited evidence.
anchor_sources: Farm Security Administration photograph collection (Library of Congress)
Social Security Act of 1935 (National Archives)
Federal Writers' Project life histories (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: World War II
essential_question: How did World War II transform the United States at home and abroad?
topics: the geography and course of the war
the Holocaust and the American response
the war's end and atomic weapons
performance_task: Complete a documented inquiry on one wartime decision, weighing context, evidence, alternatives, and consequences.
anchor_sources: Executive Order 9066, 1942 (National Archives)
Korematsu v. United States, 323 U.S. 214 (1944) (Library of Congress)
Report of the Commission on Wartime Relocation and Internment of Civilians, 1982-1983 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: Cold War and Postwar America
essential_question: How did Cold War commitments abroad reshape American life at home?
topics: the Great Society, Vietnam-era controversies, Watergate, and the environmental movement
performance_task: Create a comparative analysis of two postwar policy decisions, one foreign and one domestic, using primary sources and maps.
anchor_sources: Truman Doctrine address to Congress, 1947 (National Archives)
National Security Act of 1947 (National Archives)
Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944, the G.I. Bill (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: Civil Rights in the Post-World War II Era
essential_question: How did legal, legislative, and grassroots strategies interact in movements for rights?
topics: origins of the civil rights movement
performance_task: Analyze how legal, legislative, and grassroots strategies interacted, supporting a defensible interpretation with documents.
anchor_sources: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954) (National Archives)
Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965 (National Archives)
Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: America in a New Global Age
essential_question: How do documented patterns since 1870 inform current policy debates?
topics: globalization and the United States economy
domestic political realignment, religion in politics, and partisanship
America's changing role in the world after the Cold War
performance_task: Complete the course capstone: a researched historical argument connecting one documented pattern since 1870 to a current policy debate.
anchor_sources: Immigration and Nationality Act Amendments of 1965, the Hart-Celler Act (National Archives)
United States Census Bureau population and economic series (census.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)

subject: social-studies
title: Foundations of World Historical and Geographical Inquiry
essential_question: How do world historians and geographers make sense of a global past?
performance_task: Build an inquiry toolkit that applies periodization, scale, and corroboration to one world-historical question.
anchor_sources: Historical map collections (Library of Congress Geography and Map Division)
United Nations statistical series (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Hemispheric Interactions: World Religions and Trade Networks, 300-1500 CE
essential_question: How did religions and trade networks connect distant regions before 1500?
topics: growth and interactions of world religions
performance_task: Map and explain one trade or religious network using sources that show more than one regional perspective.
anchor_sources: Historical maps of Afro-Eurasian trade routes (Library of Congress Geography and Map Division)
Digitized manuscript collections of medieval travel accounts (British Library and Library of Congress digital collections)

subject: social-studies
title: Dar al-Islam, the Mongols, and the Americas
essential_question: How did large political and cultural systems organize power and exchange?
topics: growth of Islam and Dar al-Islam
spheres of interaction in the Americas
performance_task: Compare two large political or cultural systems using evidence about governance, exchange, and consequence.
anchor_sources: Digitized regional and empire maps, 1200-1500 (Library of Congress Geography and Map Division)
Published archaeological site reports for Mesoamerican and Andean centers (Smithsonian Institution)

subject: social-studies
title: The Emergence of the First Global Age
essential_question: How did separate regional systems become one connected global system?
topics: new maritime trade routes and commercial networks
performance_task: Explain how a global system emerged, using maps and sources from at least two regions.
anchor_sources: Early modern world maps and portolan charts (Library of Congress Geography and Map Division)
East India Company records (British Library, India Office Records)
Dutch East India Company (VOC) records (Nationaal Archief, The Hague)

subject: social-studies
title: Cultural Encounters, the Columbian Exchange, and the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade
essential_question: What were the human and environmental consequences of global encounter?
performance_task: Produce a dignity-centered, source-based analysis of the human and environmental consequences of global encounter.
anchor_sources: Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database (slavevoyages.org)
Published narratives of formerly enslaved people held in the Library of Congress Rare Book collections
Spanish colonial administrative records (Archivo General de Indias, Seville, via PARES)

subject: social-studies
title: Global Revolutions, Migration, and Interconnection
essential_question: What made the long nineteenth century an age of global revolution and movement?
topics: characteristics and extent of global revolutions
performance_task: Analyze one revolution or migration using quantitative evidence and at least two perspectives.
anchor_sources: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, 1789 (Avalon Project)
International migration statistics in Ferenczi and Willcox, International Migrations (National Bureau of Economic Research, 1929-1931)

subject: social-studies
title: Nationalism, Industrialization, and Imperialism Compared
essential_question: Why did industrialization and imperialism produce such different outcomes across regions?
topics: comparing political revolutions and independence movements
performance_task: Build a comparative case study of two societies experiencing industrialization or imperial rule.
anchor_sources: General Act of the Berlin Conference on West Africa, 26 February 1885 (published treaty series; digitized copies at the Internet Archive)
Historical industrial production and trade series in Mitchell, International Historical Statistics, together with national census and trade returns

subject: social-studies
title: Global Crisis and Achievement, 1900-Present
essential_question: How did the twentieth century produce both unprecedented destruction and unprecedented cooperation?
topics: power, resistance, and the changing nature of global conflict
World War I and the interwar period
World War II and its global course
performance_task: Complete a documented inquiry that compares the nature and impact of two twentieth-century conflicts and distinguishes genocide from other atrocities using accurate definitions and cited sources.
anchor_sources: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide, 1948 (United Nations Digital Library)
Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948 (United Nations Digital Library)
Charter of the United Nations, 1945 (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Contemporary Global Issues
essential_question: How do world-historical patterns shape the global issues we face now?
topics: connecting historical patterns to present issues
performance_task: Complete the course capstone: a geographic and historical investigation of one contemporary global issue with maps, data, and cited multi-regional sources.
anchor_sources: United Nations population and development statistical series (United Nations Digital Library)
Paris Agreement, 2015 (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Philosophical Foundations of Civic Society and Government
essential_question: How can a government protect individual rights and pursue the common good at the same time?
topics: unalienable rights and the common good
forms and limits of political authority
performance_task: Design and defend a governance framework that balances rights and the common good, citing foundational arguments accurately.
anchor_sources: Declaration of Independence (National Archives)
Constitution of the United States (National Archives)
The Federalist Papers (Avalon Project)

subject: social-studies
title: Founding and Development of American Government
essential_question: How do Democratic Values and Constitutional Principles work together, and where do they collide?
topics: influential speeches, writings, cases, and laws
performance_task: Trace one Democratic Value from a founding document through a later case or law, citing each source accurately.
anchor_sources: The Federalist Papers (Avalon Project)
Anti-Federalist essays, including the Brutus and Federal Farmer letters (Library of Congress digital collections)
Bill of Rights (National Archives)
Declaration of Sentiments, 1848 (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Structure and Function of Governments in the United States
essential_question: How do the branches and levels of American government compete and cooperate to make policy?
topics: the legislative branch and the power of the purse
the executive branch and the federal bureaucracy
the judicial branch and judicial review
federalism and the division of powers
state, local, and tribal governments, revenue, and direct democracy
parties, media, interest groups, and other civic actors
performance_task: Trace one policy from proposal to implementation across branches and levels of government, documenting each step, its funding source, and the civic actors who shaped it.
anchor_sources: Constitution of the United States, Articles I-III (National Archives)
Constitution of the State of Michigan, 1963 (Michigan Legislature)
Congressional and state legislative records (congress.gov and legislature.mi.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Rights and Liberties in the United States
essential_question: When may government limit a right, and who decides?
topics: application of the Bill of Rights
extensions of civil rights and civil liberties
tensions among liberty, order, and equality
limits on rights and their justification
performance_task: Analyze a rights conflict using the constitutional text, the reasoning of decided cases, and at least two fairly represented positions.
anchor_sources: Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment (National Archives)
Published opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States (supremecourt.gov and Library of Congress)
Civil Rights Act of 1964 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: The United States in World Affairs and Citizenship in Action
essential_question: How do citizens and institutions shape what the United States does at home and abroad?
topics: formation and implementation of United States foreign policy
the United States role in international institutions and affairs
rights and responsibilities in civic society
civic inquiry, public policy, civic action, and public discourse
performance_task: Complete the civics performance task: a public-issue analysis with a documented, lawful, and feasible civic action plan.
anchor_sources: Charter of the United Nations, 1945 (United Nations Digital Library)
Immigration and Nationality Act and naturalization requirements (U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services)
Federal Register rules and notices (federalregister.gov) and public rulemaking dockets (regulations.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The Market Economy: Scarcity, Decisions, and Competition

anchor_sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics data series (bls.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)

subject: social-studies
title: Prices, Markets, and the Role of Government
essential_question: What happens to prices, quantities, and people when government acts in a market?

anchor_sources: Consumer Price Index and producer price series (bls.gov)
Federal budget and tax documents (U.S. Government Publishing Office, govinfo.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The National Economy
essential_question: What do national economic indicators actually tell us, and what do they hide?
performance_task: Interpret a set of real economic indicators and defend a claim about national economic conditions, naming the limits of each measure.
anchor_sources: Gross domestic product and national accounts (Bureau of Economic Analysis, bea.gov)
Employment situation and price index releases (bls.gov)
Federal Open Market Committee statements (federalreserve.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The International Economy and Personal Finance
essential_question: How do global markets and personal financial choices affect each other?
topics: exchange rates, tariffs, and trade barriers
performance_task: Complete the course capstone: a two-part defense pairing an economic policy analysis with a personal financial decision model.
anchor_sources: International trade statistics (census.gov and United Nations Digital Library)
Consumer financial disclosure and education materials (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, consumerfinance.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Research Design and the Arc of Inquiry
essential_question: What makes a research question worth asking and actually answerable?
performance_task: Produce a reviewed research proposal with a compelling question, supporting questions, candidate sources, methods, and ethical safeguards.
anchor_sources: C3 Framework for Social Studies State Standards (National Council for the Social Studies)
Michigan K-12 Social Studies Standards, Arc of Inquiry, grades 9-12 (Michigan Department of Education)

subject: social-studies
title: Historiography and Contested Interpretation
essential_question: Why do capable historians reach different conclusions from the same evidence?
topics: identifying an author's argument and evidence
comparing competing accounts of one event
performance_task: Write a historiographic analysis comparing at least three published interpretations of one event, attributing each argument accurately.
anchor_sources: Peer-reviewed historical journals available through public and university library access
Published review essays and bibliographic guides (Library of Congress research guides)

subject: social-studies
title: Advanced Source Criticism and Evidence Standards
essential_question: How do you establish that a source is what it claims to be?
topics: distinguishing primary and secondary sources at scale
performance_task: Build an annotated source dossier documenting provenance, reliability, and corroboration for every source in your capstone.

Published citation standards (Chicago Manual of Style; Modern Language Association handbook)

subject: social-studies
title: Comparative Government and Constitutional Design

Charter of the United Nations and member state documentation (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Geospatial and Quantitative Analysis for Social Science
essential_question: What can maps and data honestly show, and where do they mislead?
performance_task: Produce a map-and-data analysis that states its methods, limitations, and uncertainty explicitly.
anchor_sources: United States Census Bureau data and geographic files (census.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)
United Nations population and development statistics (United Nations Digital Library)

subject: social-studies
title: Applied Economics and Policy Analysis
essential_question: How do you compare policy options when every option has costs?

anchor_sources: Congressional Budget Office cost estimates and reports (cbo.gov)
Government Accountability Office program evaluations (gao.gov)
Federal Register rules and notices (federalregister.gov)

title: Scoping the Capstone Issue: Contemporary Global and National Investigation

Congressional Research Service reports (crsreports.congress.gov)

title: Public Discourse, Deliberation, and Argument from Evidence

topics: representing opposing positions at their strongest
rules of evidence in public debate
revising a position under new evidence

Public rulemaking comment dockets (regulations.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Capstone: Independent Research, Civic Action, and Public Defense
essential_question: Can you defend your own conclusion to someone who has not agreed to be persuaded?
topics: reflection and transfer beyond the course
performance_task: Complete the senior capstone: an independent research argument, a documented civic action, and a defense that answers unrehearsed questions.
source_focus: the learner's own annotated source dossier
public records relevant to the action
anchor_sources: The learner's annotated source dossier assembled in Unit 3
Public records and correspondence generated by the learner's civic action
